text: Measured directly in the brain (7Li magnetic resonance spectroscopy, a small study of two volunteers at steady state), lithium's median half-life was 28 h there against 16 h in serum: the brain clears it more slowly than the blood does.
title: The brain lets go of lithium more slowly

text: Measured in post-mortem brain tissue of 11 treated patients (one small study, a population estimate), haloperidol sat at 10 to 30 times its optimal serum level and left the brain with a half-life of 6.8 days, against hours in the blood: its effects can outlast the last dose by weeks.
title: The brain lets go of haloperidol far more slowly

text: Paroxetine is a mechanism-based ("suicide") inhibitor of CYP2D6, the isoform that clears it: it inactivates its own route of elimination. Plasma levels therefore rise faster than the dose, and the substrate + inhibitor rows below describe a moving target rather than a fixed rate.
title: Non-linear pharmacokinetics

text: MDMA inhibits the CYP2D6 that metabolises it (autoinhibition), so clearance saturates as the dose rises: kinetics become zero-order, and repeated doses give disproportionately higher, longer-lasting levels. The substrate row below is the mechanism, not the rate.
title: Non-linear pharmacokinetics

text: Nearly every pathway below is drawn twice, once in each hemisphere, because we assume the left and right brain are wired the same way. The sources describe a tract once, without saying which side, so the dataset stores one arrow and the viewer mirrors it onto the other hemisphere. No quote backs that mirrored copy, and a real pathway can be stronger on one side (lateralization). A mirrored pair counts as one node here, not two.
title: Left/right symmetry is assumed

text: Each row above is sourced on its own, but the list is not: it holds the routes a source here happens to name, and no corpus claims to name them all. An isoform missing from it means no source stated that route, never that the drug avoids it. The interactions below are derived from this same list, so an unnamed shared route is simply an interaction nothing draws.
title: Not the full set of routes
